sheet.tagline: Opposite ends or same direction — drop a nested loop.

patterns.title: Opposite ends
patterns.summary: Start L=0, R=n−1. Move the end that makes the sum closer to the target. Sorting (if allowed) is the enabling step.

patterns.title: Fast & slow (same array)
patterns.summary: Slow marks the boundary of the kept region; fast explores. Same skeleton as array write-pointer drills.

patterns.title: Inward area search
patterns.summary: Width shrinks as pointers meet — only move the shorter side, because moving the taller one cannot improve the min.

patterns.title: Two-list merge walk
patterns.summary: Always take the smaller head. When one list exhausts, append the rest. Linear in combined length.

traps.title: Forgetting the sort prerequisite
traps.detail: Opposite-end sum logic is wrong on unsorted data. Either sort first (and handle index requirements) or pick another pattern.

traps.title: Crossing pointers
traps.detail: Loop condition is usually L < R. Equality can double-count the middle element — know whether the problem allows it.
